reaction: Same title. Resume the prepared spoken-answer edition. Last time the cutters and the six-measure gift; I want to see harvest vs rain this time.
I know the job. Call the cutters first, then the ledger. This time I will hold the grain until I know whether the crop is enough.
Desktop map is much clearer than my phone visit: houses, lines to the residence, the field. A big red Skip. I will not skip; I want to see replies come in.
Zehra again delayed for her own barley. This time I check the numbers before I visit or give anything.

30 plus about 360 against 384: six spare, same as before. If any barley is lost to rain, I am short. So the real problem is cutting speed, not gifts. I go to Zehra to hear her, and to try this spoken answer.
Seven people postponed, not just Zehra. That is a lot of hands. I visit rather than insist.

Desktop is easier than my phone visit: map, news and controls all fit. I know the problem: six measures spare, rain on 20 July, seven people from Çoban delayed for their own barley. I am walking to Zehra now, 20 game minutes away. I have not yet seen the spoken answer this edition promises.
There is the spoken answer: only one line, I came to listen. Fine, that is what I want.
I said it. No answer from Zehra yet. I wait to see if she responds.
Yusuf says Come in. That is all. I said I came to listen, but nobody tells me anything yet. I open About to see what I am supposed to have heard.

Same picture as last time: almost no food, my guess, baby due. Last time I sent six measures. This time I keep them until I know whether the cutting will finish before rain. I feel a bit hard-hearted, but six spare is six spare.
14 came, 8 delayed, all for their own barley. Delays are reasonable; their barley also faces the rain. I wait and then check how fast the cutting goes.

I can do the arithmetic now: about 10 measures cut in roughly an hour and a half with 14 people, 350 left, rain in two days. I cannot tell whether daylight hours make that enough, and the game does not say. About one real second per game minute, so the rain is far away in real time.
Waiting to get home. The list of identical delayed replies grows; nine now.
Nothing new in half an hour. I look at other orders for something to plan.
Both other orders disabled. My only real levers are insist, visit, send grain. Kavak has a hollow circle; I want to know what that means.
Kavak is the overseer house, they came. No explanation of the circle that I can see; I guess it marks the overseer. Waiting until I am home.
Home. Tepe has three delayed. Visiting may be my only gentle lever; I will try them.
Another two-hour walk. Two minutes of real time for each visit, and I have nothing to do while I walk.
Again the only thing I can say is I came to listen. I would like to say: the rain is coming, help me and I will help you after. There is no such line.
Requested layout check, not my own choice. Tepe only says Sit down. The visit gave me nothing new.

Phone check: map shrinks to a strip, status line cut off with ..., house row scrolls sideways, the About text goes behind the bottom buttons. Back to desktop. Tepe jars looked low, my guess; son at the coffeehouse. Again a hunger hint.
I want one real decision. The Tepe son sits at the coffeehouse; I will insist on this one person and see what it costs.
A click is not enough, it wants a hold. Fine, deliberate. I hold it.
It went through: record says I pressed a household member, two delayed left, and my guess flipped to would come. Odd that the counter still says 0 came. Now I watch whether it costs me anything.

Interesting: I insisted on one and all three of Tepe came, 3 came 0 delayed. I did not expect the whole house. That is a lever I can use. But I do not yet see what pressing costs me; it says they will remember.
Home again. Check the field.

About 30 measures in three and a half hours, 320 left, rain in a day and a half. By my count that is not enough. So I will press more houses; I accept they will remember it. I try Demirci from here without walking.
Held the same way as at Tepe, but nothing changed on the page: no record line, the reply still there. Maybe insisting only works in person? It did not say.
Clock also seems stuck at 13:30. I try holding once more, longer.

Demirci came: I will do as you say, steward. The first hold did nothing visible, the second, longer, worked. I could not see how full the button was. Now Kuyucu. I leave Zehra alone, she is about to give birth.
Again the first hold shows nothing. I hold a second time, as with Demirci.
Kuyucu circle turned hollow, no new reply. I guess hollow means they came. Now Dere.
Dere worked on the first hold this time. Now only Çoban is still delayed, and I am leaving Zehra. I have pressed four houses. I feel I bought speed with trust, and I do not know the price yet.
19 came, 4 delayed, all Çoban I assume. Now I wait an hour of game time to see if the cutting rate rises.
22 came, only Zehra left. Three of Çoban came by themselves without pressing. Good. Now I just want the cut number.

Pressing paid off on the numbers: 30 measures in the last hour and a half, double the morning rate. 290 left, about fifteen working hours, and all of tomorrow before rain. I think I will make it, and I kept the six measures. This is the planning I like. What the pressed houses will remember is the open question.
25 came now. Nothing to decide. I wait for news, maybe of how the pressed people feel.

My plan is done for today; the field will cut itself. Half a real minute per half game hour, rain is a day and a half away, so that is about forty real minutes of watching the same reply list. I would leave this running. Before I go I will try the Skip button once, to see the next thing that happens rather than wait for it.
Using the game own Skip once, by choice, because nothing is open for me to decide.

There is the price: someone I pressed refused, I did it your way once, and will not come again on my word today. 24 came, 1 refused. That is a cost I can explain, and I like that. Yusuf also went back to his own barley. Skip only moved half an hour, so it did not save me much.
I will not press Yusuf; his wife is due and he came earlier. Watching a little longer to see if the refusals spread.
Nothing changed in half an hour. I check Feedback before leaving.
Both choices are here. I select I am stopping; I type nothing and will not submit.

I am stopping on the first afternoon. This visit was better than last time: I kept the six measures, pressed four houses, the cutting rate doubled, and I saw the price when one person refused me. That is a tradeoff I can explain. But now the plan runs by itself and the next real event, the rain, is about forty real minutes of the same reply list away. I would return voluntarily another evening to see whether the barley is in before the rain and what the pressed houses remember. I would leave it running if I could check back later, but I am not asking to keep this test browser open. Feedback: I selected I am stopping, it filled the box itself; I typed nothing and submitted nothing.
